title: Cauliflower Cheese
subtitle: Cauliflower baked in a rich cheese sauce
excerpt: Cauliflower florets baked in a thick, mature cheddar béchamel until the top is bubbling and golden. A British side dish that is filling enough to serve as a main.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cauliflower cheese is a defining British side dish with roots in the 18th century, when imported cheese sauces were fashionable with vegetables. It remains central to the Sunday roast and is one of the most popular comfort foods in Britain. The best version uses a mature, sharp cheddar that gives the sauce enough flavour to stand up to the mild cauliflower. Cooking the cauliflower until very just tender before baking means it finishes cooking in the oven without becoming waterlogged. Some versions add bacon or mustard to the sauce. The cauliflower must be very dry before it goes into the sauce or it will make the béchamel watery.

recipeTools.notes: For the sauce and blanching the cauliflower.

content.text: Cook the cauliflower until it is just barely tender, then drain it thoroughly: excess water will make the sauce runny. A sharp, well-aged cheddar gives more flavour than a mild one. The sauce needs to be generously seasoned. Make the sauce thick enough to coat the cauliflower without running to the bottom of the dish in a pool: it will loosen slightly during baking.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Cook the cauliflower florets in a large pan of well-salted boiling water for 4 to 5 minutes until just barely tender. Drain thoroughly and spread in an oven-proof dish.

Make a béchamel: melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 2 minutes. Add the warm milk gradually, whisking until smooth. Stir over medium heat until thickened. Remove from the heat. Stir in three-quarters of the cheese, the mustard, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Pour the sauce over the cauliflower. Scatter the remaining cheese over the top. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until bubbling and golden brown. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
